newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand and bonds ended sharply firmer on Friday on the back of President Nelson Mandela's opening address to parliament which financial markets viewed as positive although short on concrete details.

Currency and bond dealers said they expected the markets to continue bullish next week and in the period leading up to the March budget in which players expected government's macro-economic plans to be fleshed out.

Trade was quieter towards the close following a hectic morning just before and after Mandela's 0900 GMT speech to parliament in Cape Town in which he reaffirmed the government's commitment to a phased removal of foreign exchange controls.

Dealers said that commitment as well as pledges on privatisation helped boost the rand to below the 4.44 level against the dollar at noon to its strongest level in 6-1/2 months of 4.4390. It later trade, it firmed further, touching 4.43 bid from 4.4750/4780 at Thursday's close.

"There was positive market activity as a result of President Mandela's speech. I think the market probably discounted a positive view from the president earlier as there was hectic activity just before his address," one currency dealer said.
"His commitment to the relaxation of foreign exchange controls led to further positive sentiment, especially internationally," she added.
Another trader said she saw the rand bottoming out at the psychologically important 4.40 level on the dollar in the next couple of weeks before the budget on March 12.
However, both currency and bond dealers said there was some disappointment that Mandela failed to meet market expectations of bold steps on exchange controls.

"There were no fireworks in Mandela's speech. It's a pity there were no concrete details but as long as the commitment is there to tackle these issues sentiment will remain strong," one bond dealer said.
The dealer said firmer U.S. bonds as well as expectations of improved January gold and foreign exchange reserves due at 1600 GMT had also bolstered sentiment on the local market.
"The markets are looking good and should continue on the same path next week," another one said.
The benchmark R150 was yielding 14.99 percent at Friday's close, down from 15.04 pct at 1405 GMT on Thursday.
Dealers said the rand and bonds had been feeding on each other recently, with a buoyant rand luring overseas buyers back into South African debt and heavy bond buying lifting the currency.
Foreigners were once again heavy buyers of South African bonds on Thursday, taking a net 340.83 million rands worth. Net foreign purchases this year now amount to more than 3.2 billion rand.
Nominal cumulative turnover was 49.2 billion rand on Thursday -- a settlement date -- from 12.8 billion rand on Wednesday.
On the currency crosses, the rand closed Friday at 7.2175/2268 on sterling from 7.3017/3111 previously and at 0.3760/3765 on the mark versus 0.3689/3692.
On the money market, three-month NCDs were quoted unchanged from Thursday's 16.50 percent offered level and the 90-day BA rate was also steady at between 15.80 to 16.05 percent bid.
The money market shortage slipped to 9.571 billion rand on Thursday from 9.736 billion rand on Wednesday, the Reserve Bank said.
